summary: On the final day of the window, Bitcoin lost a third of its value within 24 hours, a sudden and severe single-day drawdown in a widely-traded asset. This kind of abrupt repricing is exactly the sort of event that a purely price/volatility-based statistical model would flag as a regime change.
mechanism: A one-third intraday loss in a major, liquid, actively-traded asset produces an extreme spike in realized volatility and a large negative return shock, which is precisely the signature a price-and-volatility-only model is designed to detect as a change in market conditions.

claims.claim: Bitcoin lost a third of its value within a 24-hour period on Day 14, the day the model flagged.

competing_explanation: Other Day 14 items (Apple facing lawsuits over throttling older iPhones, Abbas rejecting a US peace plan, unclear coalition outcomes in unnamed elections, UK passport announcement) are politically or corporately notable but lack the direct, large-magnitude price/volatility signature that a statistical model monitoring only price and volatility data would react to; none of them describes a market-wide financial shock comparable to the Bitcoin crash.
